settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: ACCEPTED_PATTERN still restricts the character set to alphanumerics, '.', ']', '[', '_', "'" and whitespace; many OGNL metacharacters such as '#', '@', '(', ')', '=', '*', '$' are rejected, which limits expression construction.
Matching is done with matcher.matches() (full-string), not find(), so the whole cookie name must consist solely of allowed characters.
Exploitability depends on application/deployment interceptor configuration; the cookie interceptor is not necessarily in the default stack.

ParametersInterceptor shows the framework elsewhere does enforce class-access exclusion and deny-method-execution, so the gap may be intentional configuration-dependent behavior rather than a runtime-reachable flaw.
candidates.description: CookieInterceptor.intercept() iterates over all request cookies and, when the cookie name matches the configured cookiesName set (including the wildcard '*' case), calls populateCookieValueIntoStack(), which unconditionally executes stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue) (lines 273-274 and 284-285). stack.setValue on the ValueStack interprets the supplied name as an OGNL expression/chain, so a cookie name such as a dotted/indexed property path is turned into an OGNL assignment on the action. The only filter is isAcceptableName(), which matches the name against ACCEPTED_PATTERN = "[a-zA-Z0-9\\.\\]\\[_'\\s]+" (line 170) via acceptedPattern.matcher(name).matches() (line 249). This pattern permits dot, bracket, underscore, single-quote and whitespace characters, i.e. the building blocks of OGNL property/subscript expressions, and unlike ParametersInterceptor this interceptor never applies ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN and never sets ReflectionContextState.DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION. The removed class-access check is even documented in the comment at line 248. Compare with ParametersInterceptor, which routes every parameter name through acceptableName() -> isExcluded() using ExcludedPatterns.EXCLUDED_PATTERNS compiled with CASE_INSENSITIVE (lines 416-462, 502-506) and sets deny-method-execution plus MemberAccessValueStack accept/exclude properties (lines 241-250, 314-328). This is a candidate root cause: cookie-controlled names reach setValue with a weaker guard than the parameter path.
missing_evidence: No concrete OGNL payload was demonstrated end-to-end, and no test/exploit in the repo proves a cookie name can achieve method execution or class access.
HttpServletRequest.getCookies() behavior for crafted cookie names (container parsing, quoting, allowed characters) was not verified.
The configured cookie-interceptor instances in shipped struts.xml/struts-plugin.xml stacks were not enumerated to confirm a wildcard cookiesName deployment.

Whether ValueStack.setValue here honors any additional allowlist (e.g. via the action's ParameterNameAware or MemberAccessValueStack) for the cookie path was not confirmed; no such call was seen in CookieInterceptor.
The OGNL version in use (pom.xml ognl.version 3.0.6) and any evaluator-level expression restrictions were not examined.
preconditions: An action (or its interceptor stack) is configured with the cookie interceptor and cookiesName contains '*' or the attacker-chosen cookie name (so the name passes the cookiesNameSet test at lines 227/232).
cookiesValue is empty or '*' (the default documented behavior), so populateCookieValueIntoStack always writes to the stack (lines 262-274).
The servlet container accepts a crafted cookie name (dotted/indexed/quoted form) and exposes it through HttpServletRequest.getCookies() (line 218).
candidates.title: CookieInterceptor injects cookie names/values into the OGNL value stack without the ExcludedPatterns / class-access guard used by ParametersInterceptor

counter_evidence: The shipped default ACCEPTED_PATTERN (line 170) is restrictive, and changing configuration requires an intentional administrative action.
This is a configuration finding rather than a defect in default code paths; many frameworks expose such tuning knobs.
candidates.description: setAcceptCookieNames(String pattern) reassigns acceptedPattern = Pattern.compile(pattern) (lines 206-208) and that pattern is the sole gate used by isAcceptableName() (line 249). Because the parameter is a raw regex taken from interceptor configuration, setting acceptCookieNames to something permissive (or an unexpected value) would widen the set of cookie names that reach stack.setValue; conversely the default is the restrictive ACCEPTED_PATTERN. This is a configuration-driven trust boundary worth flagging because the whole security posture of the cookie-to-stack binding rests on this single, operator-supplied pattern, and the code performs no validation of the supplied pattern. The interceptor also exposes setCookiesName (lines 184-187) and setCookiesValue (lines 196-199) which control which cookies are propagated at all.
missing_evidence: No shipped struts.xml/struts-plugin.xml was found configuring a permissive acceptCookieNames value.
No documentation/test shows the intended range of accepted patterns or whether deployment-time validation exists.
preconditions: An application configures the cookie interceptor's acceptCookieNames with a permissive or unintended regular expression (e.g. a copy/paste or wildcard pattern).
cookiesName includes '*' or the targeted cookie name, so matching cookie names are propagated to stack.setValue.
candidates.title: CookieInterceptor acceptCookieNames pattern is fully configurable and replaces the built-in name guard
